record.paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
record.original_question: For a homogeneous Riemannian space (M=G/K,g) that is not a g.o. space, explicitly describe the homogeneous geodesics it does have. Equivalently, determine which nonzero vectors X in the Lie algebra of G make gamma(t)=exp(tX).o a geodesic, and give an effective method for computing these geodesic vectors even when not every geodesic of M is homogeneous.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M = G/K, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ be a reductive decomposition of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$, where $\mathfrak{k}$ is the Lie algebra of $K$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ is an $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement identified with the tangent space $T_o M$. A nonzero vector $X \in \mathfrak{g}$ is called a geodesic vector if the curve $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\cdot o$ is a geodesic of $(M,g)$. The space $(M,g)$ is called a g.o. (geodesic orbit) space if every geodesic through $o$ is of the form $\exp(tX)\cdot o$ for some $X \in \mathfrak{g}$.

Assume that $(M=G/K, g)$ is not a g.o. space. The problem is the following:

(a) Explicitly describe the homogeneous geodesics that $(M,g)$ does possess, i.e., determine the set
$$ \mathcal{V}(G/K, g) = \{ X \in \mathfrak{g} \setminus \{0\} : t \mapsto \exp(tX)\cdot o \text{ is a geodesic of } (M,g)\}. $$

(b) Provide an effective algorithmic method (in terms of the Lie bracket structure of $\mathfrak{g}$, the decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$, and the inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$ induced by $g$) for computing $\mathcal{V}(G/K, g)$ in the case when $(M,g)$ is not a g.o. space, i.e., when not every geodesic of $M$ arises in this way.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature contains the standard geodesic-vector criterion (Kowalski–Vanhecke) and explicit determinations of homogeneous geodesics in many specific classes (flag manifolds, certain Finsler and Randers spaces, sub-Riemannian settings), but no general effective classification of the set of geodesic vectors for arbitrary non-g.o. homogeneous Riemannian spaces appears to have been established. The problem is posed as an open program of describing such geodesics case by case, and current sources show only partial progress in special families.

status_evidence.title: Compact Riemannian Manifolds with Homogeneous Geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies homogeneous geodesics on compact homogeneous spaces; provides partial results and criteria via geodesic vectors.
status_evidence.claim: General description of homogeneous geodesics on non-g.o. spaces is treated only in particular cases.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Manifolds and Homogeneous Geodesics (Springer book)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive monograph on g.o. spaces and homogeneous geodesics; classification results given mainly for special classes.
status_evidence.claim: No general effective algorithm is given for arbitrary non-g.o. spaces.

status_evidence.title: Two-step homogeneous geodesics in some homogeneous Finsler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work extending homogeneous-geodesic analysis to specific Finsler examples.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues in special cases rather than a general solution.
